## Correction Operation Verbs [WORKING CANON — full definitions now live in `meta/lexicon` §XI]

`meta/lexicon` was briefly missing this section after an accidental deletion; it has been restored and the verb list below was folded into it as §XI (Correction Operation Verbs), with a usage note on when narration should name the operation versus simply show it. Do not duplicate the full definitions here — this is a pointer plus the one-line index for quick reference.

| Verb | One-line gloss |
|---|---|
| Sever | Remove a relationship entirely (Tomas ↔ Halloway) |
| Attach | Establish a relationship that did not previously exist (Mercer ↔ Halloway client) |
| Reconcile | Alter dependent relationships so a correction remains stable |
| Redirect | Move an existing relationship onto a different valid carrier (sever + attach, common enough to name) |
| Attenuate | Weaken a relationship without removing it (distinct from Bloomrot-propagation "attenuation," `meta/lexicon` §VI) |
| Reinforce | Increase the stability or authority of an existing relationship |
| Constrain | Preserve a relationship but restrict what it may imply or cause |
| Partition | Split a compound relationship into independently actionable parts |
| Bind | Make one relationship conditional on another |
| Substitute | Replace one carrier with another while preserving selected dependent relationships |
| Anchor | Designate a relationship that must survive other corrections |
| Isolate | Prevent a relationship from propagating consequences without necessarily severing it |
| Release | Deliberately remove a previously imposed constraint, binding, isolation, or correction pressure |

**Already demonstrated in drafted prose:** `bloomrot_v2/chapter_1` shows sever/attach/reconcile/redirect narrated in plain language during Noor and B's Tomas Vale discussion ("You severed what could no longer remain. You attached what still needed somewhere to belong. You reconciled the damage..."). `bloomrot_v2/chapter_2` shows partition and bind performed but not named — B separates "available/present/contact/continuous" (partition) and ties contact to active need (bind) without Mote or B using the technical term. Per the usage note in `meta/lexicon` §XI, this is correct: partition/bind/anchor/isolate may be named directly in a future scene where a character is speaking in strict professional register (e.g., a Continuity-division report on the Morrow Stack correction), but chapter_2 itself earns the plain-language version because it is written from B's working perspective, not a technical filing.
